articles.title: Bengaluru's second airport awaits state proposal despite AAI study
articles.description: AAI has completed pre-feasibility studies for three shortlisted sites, but the Centre says it is yet to receive Karnataka's formal proposal under the Greenfield Airports Policy. The proposal to build a second international airport for Bengaluru has moved into an important stage, but the project cannot progress further until the Karnataka government submits a formal proposal to the Union government. The Centre has confirmed that while the Airports Authority of India (AAI) has already completed the pre-feasibility study for three shortlisted locations, it has not yet received any official application under the Greenfield Airports Policy. The update was shared by Minister of State for Civil Aviation Murlidhar Mohol in the Lok Sabha while replying to an unstarred question raised by Bengaluru Central MP P C Mohan. According to the minister, the AAI has already forwarded its pre-feasibility study report to the Karnataka government after evaluating the three shortlisted sites. However, no further proposal has been submitted either by the Karnataka government or by any airport developer. The issue gained attention after P C Mohan questioned the Centre about the status of Bengaluru's second airport project. He sought details on the shortlisted locations, including sites along Kanakapura Road and Kunigal Road, the extent of land identified for the project, the completion of the feasibility study, the expected timeline for final approval and construction, and future expansion plans for the existing Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). Also Read: Heavy rain alert for coastal, Malnad Karnataka; Orange Alert in Dakshina Kannada Responding to these queries, the Civil Aviation Ministry clarified that the next step now rests with the Karnataka government. The Centre stated that it has not received any proposal after the pre-feasibility report was submitted, preventing further processing of the project under the Greenfield Airports Policy. The ministry also provided an update on the capacity of Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). At present, the airport has an annual passenger handling capacity of 51.5 million passengers per annum (MPPA). During the current financial year 2026-27 (up to June 2026), the airport has recorded an average daily passenger footfall of around 1.23 lakh passengers, reflecting continued growth in both domestic and international travel. The minister also noted that the airport's average daily handling capacity is around 1.41 lakh passengers. To meet future demand, KIA is undergoing a major expansion. The airport's overall passenger handling capacity is expected to increase to 80 million passengers per annum by 2030. A significant part of this expansion will come through Phase 2 of Terminal 2, which will increase the terminal's capacity from 25 MPPA to 45 MPPA. Also Read: Peenya Flyover to stay closed at night till August 5 Meanwhile, the Karnataka government has already begun preparatory work for the proposed second airport. Earlier this year, Industries Minister M B Patil announced that the state had floated a tender inviting firms to prepare a detailed feasibility and strategy report after the AAI completed inspections of the shortlisted sites. Following the Centre's reply in Parliament, P C Mohan also highlighted on social media that the Karnataka government is yet to send its proposal for the second airport to the Union government, urging the state to take the next step so that the project can move forward. The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has completed pre-feasibility studies for three sites for Bengaluru’s second airport and submitted the report to the Government of Karnataka. The Union Government has not received any proposal thereafter from the State Government. pic.twitter.com/QmSyOmaxrl — P C Mohan (@PCMohanMP) July 27, 2026 For now, the future of Bengaluru's second international airport depends on the Karnataka government's submission of its formal proposal. Until that happens, the project will remain at the pre-feasibility stage, while expansion of Kempegowda International Airport continues to address the city's growing passenger demand.
